title: Edge vs VPC TCO scenarios - scratchpad
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working scratchpad for comparing TCO/ROI across small-to-medium on‑prem (customer datacenter), VPC-hosted private deployment, and a lightweight edge offering. Primary readers: product owners for Private, Solutions Eng, Sales AE for enterprise prospects, and finance lead for pricing bundles.

High-level objective:
Create a compact, reproducible scenario matrix (1Y and 3Y) that captures: capital vs operating distinction, licensing + support bundles, uplift factors for managed services, and sensitivity to utilisation and headcount for ops. This is intentionally pragmatic — not a complete audit.

Executive summary (short):
- For mid-sized customers (peak concurrency ~80 requests/s, avg tokens 120), VPC gives lower near-term uplift and fastest time-to-value.
- On‑prem can be cheaper after year 2 only when customers amortize hardware at >= 36 months and run at sustained GPU utilization > 55%.
- Edge (small footprint appliances) is a niche addition for isolated sites; higher per-unit support cost but valuable for regulated use-cases.
- Bundled licensing + 24/7 Premium Support for Private adds ~12–18% surcharge vs base license; add managed ops pass-through for full service.

Key modeling assumptions (change these per-customer):
- Discount rate (for NPV): 8% annual.
- Hardware list price (reference): A100-class equivalent node = $18k per GPU; typical rack = 8xA100 = $144k + networking/storage => $200k rack fully populated.
- VPC monthly infrastructure (hosted in customer account) cost estimate: $/hour approx equivalent to 4xA100 share per cluster node; we model normalized hourly cost = $6.50/hr per GPU-equivalent (including infra premium).
- Redwood license: Annual per‑GPU license tiered: $30k/GPU/year base for private on-prem; VPC license is 10% lower (managed infra less friction) in these scenarios.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours) = 10% of license; Premium (24/7 + SLA) = 18% of license. Managed Ops add-on (optional) = $15k/month for small clusters or 20% of license value for larger.
- Ops headcount: on‑prem requires dedicated 0.5–1.2 FTEs for infra/ops depending on scale. We price infra engineer fully loaded at $180k/year (~$110/hr loaded).
- Utilization patterns: low (25% GPU utilization), medium (45%), high (70%).

Compact 1Y sample scenario (Mid-market cluster):
- Workload: 80 req/s peak, average request 120 tokens, steady-state daytime utilization ~45%.
- On‑prem config: 2 racks (~16 GPUs effective capacity, amortized), hardware CAPEX = $400k, annual HW maintenance & power + facility = $48k. Redwood license = $30k/GPU/year * 16 = $480k. Support (Premium) = 18% of license = $86.4k. Ops FTEs = 0.8 * $180k = $144k.
- VPC config: Equivalent capacity leased: license discount 10% => $432k. Infra consumption (cloud/VPC cost) = equivalent of $6.5/hr * 16 GPUs * 24 * 365 = $912k. Redwood managed infra discount (negotiate) assumed 10% off infra cost if committed. Support Premium = $77.76k. Managed Ops add-on optional = $180k/year.

One-year totals (rounded):
- On‑prem: CAPEX amortized 3 years => year1 HW amortization = $133k; license $480k; support $86k; ops $144k; opex (power/network) $48k => total year1 ~ $892k.
- VPC: license $432k; infra $912k (before negotiated discount); support $78k; managed ops $0 or $180k if added => total year1 ~ $1.42M (without managed ops) or ~$1.6M (with).

 -> Interpretation: VPC shows higher direct infra spending in year 1 due to cloud hourly costs; license is slightly lower. On‑prem requires CAPEX but lower opex at this scale if utilization stays above ~45%.

3-year view (simple cumulative, ignoring growth):
- On‑prem: amortized HW fully paid by Y3; year2+ lower cash outflow for infra; cumulative license+support+ops still substantial. Breakeven (cumulative) often sits between 2–3 years for medium-high utilization customers.

Sensitivity analysis notes (quick):
- GPU utilization swing +/- 10% changes effective cost per useful token by ~8–12% in on‑prem case; smaller proportional change in VPC because infra cost is more linear to usage.
- Support tier swap (Premium->Standard) reduces near-term cost 6–8% but increases MTTD risk for high-SLA customers.
- Ops FTE variation: each 0.25 FTE added increases on‑prem opex by ~$45k/year.
- Hardware price movements: a 15% drop in GPU list price shifts on‑prem breakeven earlier by ~6–12 months.

Licensing + support bundle recommendations (draft):
1) Base License (Private Core): per-GPU/year, tiered: 1–8 GPUs ($35k), 9–32 GPUs ($30k), >32 GPUs ($27k).
2) Support: Standard (10%), Business+ (14%), Premium (18%). Bundled discount when license + support bought together (1–3% depending on commit length).
3) Managed Ops Add-on: flat monthly for <16 GPU configs ($15k/mo), percent-based for larger deployments (18–22% license value).
4) Edge Appliance: single-node fixed price + annual license; support premium + remote hands priced per-incident.

Configuration guides (SRE/solutions quick rules):
- Low utilization customers (expected <35%): recommend VPC with committed discount and optional managed-ops.
- Medium utilization (35–60%): on‑prem recommended if customer can amortize HW >24 months; otherwise VPC.
- High utilization (>60% sustained): strongly consider on‑prem or Dedicated reservation (Redwood Dedicated offering) with long-term license discounts.

Open questions / data pulls required to finalize a customer quote:
- Confirm expected 95th percentile concurrency and token distribution by endpoint.
- Site power & cooling specifics for on‑prem CAPEX line items (for edge: rack/pdu constraints).
- Legal constraints affecting KMS/HSM placement (affects VPC vs on‑prem implementation complexity).
- Customer preferred amortization schedule (24 vs 36 months).

Next steps (owner: Maya / Solutions Eng):
- Convert this scratchpad to spreadsheet: separate sheets for ’Assumptions’, ’1Y scenario’, ’3Y NPV’, ’Sensitivity sweeps’. (ACTION: Diego to create base sheet template - JIRA PD-6123).
- Run two example customer pitches with real numbers (one regulated finance prospect, one gaming infra lead) and capture delta vs simple hosted API.
- Draft bundled pricing one-pager for AEs with quick decision tree (edge vs vpc vs on‑prem).

Appendix A — quick table (text) example for copy into sheet:
Scenario | Deployment | Year1 CAPEX | Year1 OPEX (license+support+ops+infra) | Year1 total
Mid-market | On‑prem | $400,000 | $492,000 | $892,000
Mid-market | VPC | $0 | $1,420,000 | $1,420,000
Edge-site | Appliance | $35,000/unit | $85,000 (support+ops) | $120,000

Appendix B — negotiation levers for sales:
- Multi-year license commitment (2–3y) for 10–18% discount.
- Minimum committed infra hours in VPC for infra discount.
- Transfer of some Ops responsibilities to customer (reduced managed-ops fee).

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to extract Redwood Dedicated internal cost model to compare properly — current VPC infra estimate is rough.
- Confirm how license should be calculated for quantized / multi-precision models (does license depend on effective GPU-equivalent or model scale?).
- Capture a 6-month growth scenario in the spreadsheet to show sensitivity to consumption ramp.

End of scratchpad.
